title: Statewise reachability does not imply a usable recovery policy under partial observability

definitions.statewise: for all x in X, there exists u in U such that Reach(x,u)
definitions.uniform_policy: there exists u in U such that for all x in X, Reach(x,u)

result: Every latent state can be recoverable under some allowed control while no single control is safe/effective for all states still compatible with the observations.
HF01_implication: Recoverability must be conditioned on the allowed actuator set U.
Biological state reachability != deployable policy reachability.
If the correct actuator depends on latent state, observer quality becomes part of the control problem rather than a reporting detail.
A broader actuator set can enlarge statewise reachability while also increasing the cost of misclassification/control selection.
behavior-only, AR-axis, mechanical, regenerative and combined control sets can have different reachable sets in the synthetic model and must not share one universal RECOVERABLE label.
observer_contract: If only statewise reachability is established, an operational recovery claim remains UNKNOWN until either (a) a uniform policy is shown to work across the compatible state set or (b) the observer discriminates the policy-relevant latent states with the required error bound.
claim_boundary: This is a control-theoretic quantifier distinction inside HF01 synthetic reasoning. It does not establish the effectiveness or safety of any real intervention class.
